_comment: Extra instructions sent to Gemini when a keyword appears in the resident's prompt. Keys are matched case-insensitively as whole words or phrases (plurals like 'buses' and 'bike lanes' match too). Values may be a string or a list of strings. Keys starting with '_' are ignored. Edit freely; the file is re-read automatically when it changes.
bus: The bus lanes occupy the outermost lanes of the street unless otherwise specified. Paint them a distinct colour (red or terracotta) with 'BUS ONLY' markings and keep the remaining general-traffic lanes.
bus lane: Bus lanes run the full visible length of the street, continuous through intersections, and keep their width consistent with the existing lanes.
bike lane: Bike lanes are placed between the sidewalk and parked cars or the kerb, are narrower than a traffic lane, painted green, and separated from traffic by a buffer or bollards.
bike: Keep cycling infrastructure continuous and connected to the existing street grid.
crosswalk: Crosswalks are high-visibility zebra stripes spanning the full roadway at the intersection corners.
tree: Street trees are planted in a regular row along the kerb line at even spacing, with realistic canopies and shadows consistent with the sun angle in the photo.
park: New parkland uses realistic grass texture, groups of trees with cast shadows, and light-coloured walking paths; keep surrounding streets and buildings unchanged.
housing: New housing matches the scale, roof style and orientation of neighbouring buildings and includes realistic roof detail and shadows; avoid towers unless asked.
apartment: Multi-family buildings should be mid-rise with courtyards or setbacks, matching the street wall of the block.
parking: When parking is removed, replace it with a coherent use (building, plaza or landscaping) that aligns to the street edge; do not leave bare rectangles.
plaza: Plazas are paved with light stone or brick patterns, include benches, trees in planters and people at a plausible density for a top-down view.
protected intersection: Protected intersections use corner refuge islands, set-back bike crossings and tightened turning radii.
